title: This Animal Has Up to 32 Babies in One Litter, the Mammal Record

scenes.text: One mother. Thirty-two babies. One litter.
The tailless tenrec of Madagascar looks like a hedgehog crossed with a shrew, about 30 centimetres long and up to two kilograms.
Most mammals manage a handful of young. A tenrec litter averages 15 to 20, and litters of 32 have been recorded.
To feed them, a female can have up to 29 nipples. Then she leads the whole troop out foraging at night.
When the dry season comes, it shuts down completely: the first tropical mammal ever found to hibernate, for months at a time.
Months asleep, thirty-two mouths awake. No other mammal comes close.

description:
The tailless tenrec of Madagascar holds the mammal record for litter size: litters average 15 to 20, and as many as 32 young have been recorded from one mother, who can have up to 29 nipples to feed them.
It was also the first tropical mammal found to hibernate, sitting out the dry season for months.
Which animal mother has the hardest job?
subject: tailless tenrec
first_comment: Young tenrecs warn each other by rubbing the quills on their backs together, a trick called stridulation. What animal record should we cover next?
